messages:
Mei: Heads-up — trace ingest cost spiked ~3x over the last 6h. Looks like high-cardinality span attributes (customer_id, batch_token, model_prompt snippets) are blowing up our trace index. Grafana panels are noisy and the trace-storage SLO alerts are firing. Need a mitigation plan: SDK redaction vs OTEL collector scrub vs gateway rewrite.

Carlos: Are these attributes attached by the runtime or by product instrumentation?

Darren: Runtime libs (gpu-batcher) attach batch_id + input_len + prompt_excerpt. We also added customer_id on a debug path. At 6k rps that created millions of unique values and spiked the index/ingest cost.

Anya: We should redact at ingestion as short-term fix. Options: 1) change SDK to send hashed_id + truncate prompt (longer term); 2) OTEL collector attributes processor to delete/hash keys (fast roll); 3) increase sampling for non-error traces. My preference: collector scrub first + short-term sampler tweak.

infra-bot: deploybot: started rollout of collector-attributes-scrub config to eu-staging -> eu-prod. Monitoring: trace-ingest-cost, trace-index-cardinality. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4821 :eyes:

Mei: Proposed collector snippet (quick patch to delete raw customer identifiers and truncate prompt) — rolling to staging now:

```yaml
processors:
  attributes/scrub:
    actions:
      - key: customer_id
        action: delete
      - key: batch_token
        action: delete
      - key: model_prompt
        action: update
        new_value: "<truncated>"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [attributes/scrub]
```

Carlos: Can we preserve debugability by hashing instead of removing? e.g. add cust_hash = sha256(customer_id)[:8] so we can correlate without exposing IDs.

Darren: Yep — attributes processor supports insert/upsert. Example we tested: 

```yaml
- key: customer_id
  action: hash
  hash: sha256
  target: cust_hash
  keep: false
```

(If your collector version doesn't have hash action we can upsert with a transform processor or hash in SDK.)

Anya: Also propose tail-sampling rule tweak: keep 100% of error traces, 1% of success traces globally, and 100% for any trace that touches the gpu-batcher span for a short window after deployment. This reduces stored volume while keeping signal.

Mei: Tail sampling policy example we plan to push:

```yaml
tail_sampling:
  policies:
    - name: error-first
      decision_wait: 30s
      policies:
        - type: error
          rate: 1.0
        - type: numeric_attribute
          key: http.status_code
          min_value: 500
          rate: 1.0
        - type: always_sample
          rate: 0.01
```

Mei: Dashboard/alert changes: adjust trace-storage SLO -> page if usage > 85% for 10m, warn at 70% for 30m. Add a Grafana panel 'trace-index-cardinality' (top n keys) and an alert that fires for sudden growth spikes. Update runbook to include quick scrub job and sampling rollback.

Darren: Another thing — APAC edge proxies had been silently dropping tracestate/baggage before. If we redact at the collector but lose traceparent upstream, correlation fails. I put an envoy filter to preserve/forward trace headers. Test with: 

curl -v -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" https://staging-gateway.redwood/api/health

sre-oncall: Confirmed header preserved in na and eu, apac had been stripping tracestate but envoy fix applied at 1804998000. Re-ran synthetic and traces stitched correctly.

Carlos: Next steps I propose: 1) finish collector scrub rollout to na-prod (infra-bot), 2) merge SDK PR to send hashed customer id and truncated prompt (tracking in PR#4830), 3) apply tail-sampling tweak in collector across regions for 48h, 4) update Grafana alerts + runbook.

Mei: Agreed. I'll file the priority ticket and assign owners. For immediate rollback plan: if we see missing debugging signal, we can toggle the attributes processor and rely on sampling changes.

Anya: One more note — metric dashboards (Prom/Grafana) might need panel rate-limiters; we've had too many label permutations showing up. Recommend adding relabeling in prometheus scrape to drop high-card labels from runtime exporters.

Mei: Thanks all — keeping this thread open for post-rollout observations. Will report back with ingestion metrics in ~30m. :thumbsup:
